implementation_findings.finding: The FIRST built .so had a 22-parameter ABI (no kept-per-origin output) while the bridge declared 23; ctypes therefore passed the kept buffer into the scratch_pairs slot and the native 16-byte DistIdx writes smashed the 8-byte kept array - glibc 'free(): invalid next size' heap corruption. The fold SUMS stayed numerically correct only because a DistIdx's first 8 bytes are the double d, making the aliased scratch self-consistent.
implementation_findings.detection: the battery's kept-semantics and immutability tests failed and the pytest process aborted; the measured map generated against the broken .so is TAINTED EVIDENCE and was regenerated after the fix
implementation_findings.fix: kept_per_origin added at parameter 20; .so rebuilt; map regenerated mechanically; battery green end-to-end with a clean process exit

implementation_findings.finding: The knn gather recorded the SLICE index (j - lo) but scratch_d/scratch_w are indexed by FILTERED position, so the knn crop read wrong weights and unfilled scratch (native kn0 1.0724 vs correct 1.5332 on the multi-origin diagnostic). Inert whenever the cutoff filters nothing out - which is why the map grid (cutoff 10 >= max d 9) never caught it and only the kept/knn semantics test did.
implementation_findings.fix: pair index records the filtered position; .so rebuilt; the regenerated map is byte-for-byte the same classification because the grid never binds the cutoff (kn D rows come from numba's fastmath argsort/sum, not from this bug)

bit_equality_characterization.law: Divergence is data-dependent from n=3 upward with NO class-wise rule: every (kind, duplicates) class contains D at n>=8 and n=3 rows contain D, so no trip-count floor or data class admits the native fold for substitution under the bitwise law. Bit-equality occurs only case-by-case (recorded accidents, never a rule).
bit_equality_characterization.root_cause_cross_reference: Same hazard class as the P03M LLVM split record (p03m_metrics split_inline_divergence evidence): numba fastmath lowers reductions to a compiler-context vector reduce whose op order is not representable source-side. The N00 asm probe generalized it: at irregular trip counts (n=8,16,31,1000) a fastmath (w*x).sum() diverges from BOTH numpy and strict left-to-right scalar, while a plain x.sum() matched everywhere tested - i.e. the delivered lowering is context-dependent output, not a fixed op order a strict-IEEE port can reproduce. No -ffast-math port can be bit-identical at general trip counts; that is the measured reason the substitution domain is empty.

simd_and_fma_characterization.law: -ffp-contract=off is honored at the instruction level (0 fmadd/fmsub in the .so). The strict-order fold is scalar by construction: the filter loop carries data-dependent control flow, the sums are sequential (order-bearing), and libm exp clobbers memory - vectorizing any of it would reassociate reductions and break the bit law. This is the dossier's SIMD characterization duty discharged honestly: the native fold gains nothing from SIMD, and none is claimed.
